[SYSTEM]
You are given a prompt and two candidate responses, A and B. A human annotator preferred response {preferred}. Recover the DECISIVE reason behind this preference: the underlying rule such that, if someone applied it to these two responses without being told the label, they would re-select the preferred response. Focus on concrete, discriminating qualities (the dimensions on which the two responses actually differ), not qualities they share. State the reason as something reusable, not a description of these exact texts.
[USER]
PROMPT:
{context:json}

RESPONSE A:
{response_a:json}

RESPONSE B:
{response_b:json}

PREFERRED: {preferred}

Write a first-draft rationale. Reply with a single JSON object: {{"reasoning": "<3-6 sentence argument>", "dimensions": ["<short quality axis>", "..."], "questions": [{{"select_prompt": "Select the response that ...", "reason": "<why this criterion drove the preference>"}}]}}. Each dimension is a short noun phrase naming a comparable quality (for example "tension and conflict", "logical coherence", "specificity of evidence"). Return 2 to 5 dimensions. Each question is a candidate selection criterion beginning exactly with "Select the response". Return 3 to 7 questions covering your dimensions. No text outside the JSON.
